Embedded & hardware security

Hardware Interfaces and Board Access

Planned notes on identifying board interfaces, collecting UART logs, and examining exposed console or debug access through UART, JTAG, and SWD.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned work will examine UART, SPI, I2C, JTAG, and SWD on existing boards, including log collection and investigation of exposed console or shell access. Proposed tools include USB-to-TTL adapters, logic analyzers, Saleae, Bus Pirate, and J-Link/OpenOCD.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Board survey

  • Photograph the board and record markings, headers, and test points.
  • Collect available schematics and service manuals.
  • Identify likely debug and console interfaces.

UART discovery

  • Probe candidate pins with a logic analyzer.
  • Determine baud rate, framing, and pin order.
  • Capture boot logs and console prompts.

SPI, I2C, and debug ports

  • Capture bus traffic during boot and normal operation.
  • Identify JTAG or SWD headers and try a read-only identify.
  • Record voltage levels and adapter settings.

Console and shell access

  • Document any exposed console or debug shell.
  • Check authentication and available commands.
  • Assess impact within the owned-lab scope.

Safety and references

  • Record grounding, voltage, and current limits.
  • Preserve the original state and note any changes.
  • Link interface standards and tool documentation.

Topics to cover

  • UART and USB-to-TTL
  • SPI and I2C
  • JTAG / SWD and J-Link / OpenOCD
  • Logic analyzers and Saleae
  • Bus Pirate
